text: Let a computer program generate only the digits 0 and 1 to form a string of binary numbers with probability of occurrence of 0 at even places be $\frac{1}{2}$ and probability of occurrence of 0 at the odd place be $\frac{1}{3}$. Then the probability that '10' is followed by '01' is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
P(0 at even place) = $\frac{1}{2}$

P(0 at odd place) = $\frac{1}{3}$

 P(1 at even place) = $\frac{1}{2}$

P(1 at odd place) = $\frac{2}{3}$

P(10 is followed by 01)

= $\left (\frac{2}{3}\times \frac{1}{2}\times \frac{1}{3}\times \frac{1}{2}\right )+\left (\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{1}{3}\times \frac{1}{2}\times \frac{2}{3}\right )$

= $\frac{1}{18}+\frac{1}{18}$

= $\frac{1}{9}$

text:
The number of solutions of the equation 

$\sin ^{-1}\left [x^{2}+\frac{1}{3}\right ]+\cos ^{-1}\left [x^{2}-\frac{2}{3}\right ]=x^{2}$, for x$\in$[$-$1, 1], and [x] denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to x, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
There are three cases possible for $x\in [-1,1]$

Case I : $x\in \left [-1,-\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\right )$

$\therefore$ $\sin ^{-1}(1)+\cos ^{-1}(0)=x^{2}$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}=\frac{π}{2}+\frac{π}{2}=π$

$\Rightarrow x=\pm \sqrt{π}$ $\to$ (Reject)

Case II : $x\in \left (-\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}},\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\right )$

$\therefore$ $\sin ^{-1}(0)+\cos ^{-1}(-1)=x^{2}$

$\Rightarrow 0+π=x^{2}$

$\Rightarrow x=\pm \sqrt{π}$ $\to$ (Reject)

Case III : $x\in \left (\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}},1\right )$

$\therefore$ $\sin ^{-1}(1)+\cos ^{-1}(0)=x^{2}$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}=π\Rightarrow x=\pm \sqrt{π}$ (Reject)

$\therefore$ No solution. Therefore, the correct answer is (1).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift

text:
If the integral 

$\int\limits _{0}^{10}\frac{[\sin 2πx]}{e^{x-[x]}}dx=αe^{-1}+βe^{-\frac{1}{2}}+γ$, where $α$, $β$, $γ$ are integers and [x] denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to x, then the value of $α$ + $β$ + $γ$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given integral

$\int\limits _{0}^{10}\frac{[\sin 2πx]}{e^{x-[x]}}dx=10\int\limits _{0}^{1}\frac{[\sin 2πx]}{e^{\{x\}}}dx$ (using property of definite in.)

$=10\left [\int\limits _{0}^{1/2}0.dx+\int\limits _{1/2}^{1}\frac{-1}{e^{x}}dx\right ]$

= $-10\left [\frac{e^{-x}}{-1}\right ]_{1/2}^{1}=10\left [e^{-1}-e^{-1/2}\right ]$

$=10e^{-1}-10e^{-1/2}$

comparing with the given relation,

$α$ = 10, $β$ = $-$10, $γ$ = 0

$α$ + $β$ + $γ$ = 0

Therefore, the correct answer is (A).

text:

solution.body:
Given,

$\lim _{θ\to 0}\frac{\tan (π\cos ^{2}θ)}{\sin (2π\sin ^{2}θ)}$

$=\lim _{θ\to 0}\frac{\tan (π-π\sin ^{2}θ)}{\sin (2π\sin ^{2}θ)}$ $\therefore$ $\left (\cos ^{2}θ=1-\sin ^{2}θ\right )$

$=\lim _{θ\to 0}\frac{-\tan (π\sin ^{2}θ)}{\sin (2π\sin ^{2}θ)}$ $\therefore$ $(\tan (π-θ)=-\tan θ)$

$=\lim _{θ\to 0}\frac{\frac{-\tan (π\sin 2θ)}{π\sin 2θ}}{\frac{\sin (2π\sin 2θ)}{2π\sin 2θ}\times 2}\left (\begin{array}{l} Asθ\to 0 \\ then\qquad \sin ^{2}θ\to 0 \end{array}\right )$

$=-\frac{1}{2}.$ $\because$ $⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} \lim _{θ\to 0}\frac{\tan θ}{θ}\to 1 \\ &\lim _{θ\to 0}\frac{\sin θ}{θ}=1 \end{array}⎞⎠⎟$

solution.body:
$\cos x(3\sin x+\cos x+3)dy=(1+y\sin x(3\sin x+\cos x+3))dx$ ..... (1)

$(3\sin x+\cos x+3)(\cos xdy-y\sin xdx)=dx$

$\int d(y.\cos x)=\int \frac{dx}{3\sin x+\cos x+3}$

$y\cos x=\int \frac{1}{3\left (\frac{2\tan \dfrac{x}{2}}{1+\tan 2\dfrac{x}{2}}\right )+\left (\frac{1-\tan 2\dfrac{x}{2}}{1+\tan 2\dfrac{x}{2}}\right )+3}$

$y\cos x=\int \frac{\sec ^{2}\frac{x}{2}}{2\tan ^{2}\frac{x}{2}+6\tan \frac{x}{2}+4}=\int \frac{\frac{1}{2}\sec ^{2}\frac{x}{2}dx}{\tan ^{2}\frac{x}{2}+3\tan \frac{x}{2}+2}$

$y\cos x=\ln \left |\frac{\tan \frac{x}{2}+1}{\tan \frac{x}{2}+2}\right |+c$

Put x = 0 & y = 0

$C=-\ln \left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=\ln (2)$

$y\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )=2\ln \left |\frac{1+\sqrt{3}}{1+2\sqrt{3}}\right |+2\ln 2$

text: Let $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ c & d \end{array}\right ]$ and $B=\left [\begin{array}{l} α \\ β \end{array}\right ]\neq \left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ]$ such that AB = B and a + d = 2021, then the value of ad $-$ bc is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The matrix $B=\left [\begin{array}{l} α \\ β \end{array}\right ]$ is a non-zero $2\times 1$ column, so $AB$ is defined, and $AB=B$ gives $(A-I)B=O$.

If $A-I$ were invertible, $B=(A-I)^{-1}O=O$, which is not the case; so

$\det (A-I)=\left |\begin{array}{ll} a-1 & b \\ c & d-1 \end{array}\right |=(a-1)(d-1)-bc=0.$

Expanding, $ad-bc-(a+d)+1=0$, so

$ad-bc=(a+d)-1=2021-1=2020.$

Hence, the answer is 2020.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift

Now, $\frac{coefficientofT_{3}}{coefficientofT_{4}}=\frac{{}^{n}C_{2}.a^{2}}{{}^{n}C_{3}.a^{3}}=\frac{3}{a(n-2)}=\frac{3}{2}$

$\Rightarrow a(n-2)=2$ .......... (i)

and $\frac{coefficientofT_{4}}{coefficientofT_{5}}=\frac{{}^{n}C_{3}.a^{3}}{{}^{n}C_{4}.a^{4}}=\frac{4}{a(n-3)}=\frac{8}{3}$

$\Rightarrow a(n-3)=\frac{3}{2}$ ........ (ii)

by (i) and (ii) $n=6,a=\frac{1}{2}$

for term independent of 'x'

$n-3r=0\Rightarrow r=\frac{n}{3}\Rightarrow r=\frac{6}{3}=2$

$T_{3}={}^{6}C_{2}\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2}x^{0}=\frac{15}{4}=3.75\approx 4$

text: Let $\vec{x}$ be a vector in the plane containing vectors $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$. If the vector $\vec{x}$ is perpendicular to $\left (3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}\right )$ and its projection on $\vec{a}$ is $\frac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}$, then the value of $|\vec{x}|^{2}$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, $\vec{x}=k(\vec{a}+λ\vec{b})$

$\vec{x}$  is perpendicular to $3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$

I. k{(2 + $λ$)3 + (2$λ$ $-$ 1)2 + (1 $-$ $λ$)($-$1) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 8$λ$ + 3 = 0

$λ=\frac{-3}{8}$

II. Also projection of $\vec{x}$ on $\vec{a}$ is $\frac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}$ therefore

$\frac{\vec{x}.\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|}=\frac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow k\left \{\frac{(\vec{a}+λ\vec{b}).\vec{a}}{\sqrt{6}}\right \}=\frac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow k\left \{6+\left (\frac{3}{8}\right )\right \}=\frac{17\times 6}{2}$

$\Rightarrow k=\frac{51}{51}\times 8$

k = 8

$\therefore$ $\vec{x}=8\left (\frac{13}{8}\hat{i}-\frac{14}{8}\hat{j}+\frac{11}{8}\widehat{k}\right )$

$=13\hat{i}-14\hat{j}+11\widehat{k}$

$|\vec{x}|^{2}=169+196+121=486$

text: Consider a set of 3n numbers having variance 4. In this set, the mean of first 2n numbers is 6 and the mean of the remaining n numbers is 3. A new set is constructed by adding 1 into each of first 2n numbers, and subtracting 1 from each of the remaining n numbers. If the variance of the new set is k, then 9k is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the first $2n$ numbers be $x_{1},\ldots ,x_{2n}$ and the remaining $n$ numbers be $y_{1},\ldots ,y_{n}$. Then $\sum x_{i}=12n$ and $\sum y_{i}=3n$, so the mean of all $3n$ numbers is $\dfrac{15n}{3n}=5$.

From the variance, $\dfrac{\sum x_{i}^{2}+\sum y_{i}^{2}}{3n}-5^{2}=4\Rightarrow \sum x_{i}^{2}+\sum y_{i}^{2}=87n$.

Mean of the new set: $\dfrac{(12n+2n)+(3n-n)}{3n}=\dfrac{16}{3}$.

Sum of squares of the new set:

$\sum (x_{i}+1)^{2}+\sum (y_{i}-1)^{2}=\sum x_{i}^{2}+\sum y_{i}^{2}+2\sum x_{i}-2\sum y_{i}+2n+n=87n+24n-6n+3n=108n$

$k=\frac{108n}{3n}-\left (\frac{16}{3}\right )^{2}=36-\frac{256}{9}=\frac{68}{9}$

So $9k=68$.

Hence, the answer is 68.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift
